description: Ground-truth relevant judgment IDs for the Lexi evaluation suite. Populate doc_ids by running eval/label_helper.py, reviewing the output, and adding the IDs of genuinely relevant judgments.
case_brief: Motor accident death claim. Commercial truck. Driver unlicensed. National Insurance Co. denying liability arguing policy is void.

supporting_precedents.description: Judgments that support the claimant — insurer must pay third-party claims despite unlicensed driver / policy breach
what_to_look_for: Section 149 Motor Vehicles Act — insurer cannot escape third-party liability
Pay-and-recover doctrine — insurer pays claimant, recovers from owner
Insurer held liable despite driver having no valid licence
Commercial vehicle / truck cases where claimant succeeded

adverse_precedents.description: Judgments that support the insurer — policy void due to fundamental breach, insurer absolved
what_to_look_for: Fundamental breach of policy condition — insurer absolved
Cases distinguishing third-party from own-damage claims where insurer escaped
Breach of licence condition treated as fundamental breach
Insurer not liable where owner knowingly employed unlicensed driver

general_relevant.description: Any judgment relevant to motor accident compensation, MACT claims, dependency calculation
what_to_look_for: Multiplier method — Sarla Verma / Second Schedule

eval_queries.query: Find precedents supporting Mrs. Lakshmi Devi's claim against the insurance company
Find adverse precedents the insurance company could use against the claimant
What compensation range is realistic for a 42-year-old with monthly income of Rs 35000?
Which judgments involve Section 149 of the Motor Vehicles Act?
Find cases discussing contributory negligence where the driver was unlicensed.
Which cases specifically discuss the 'pay and recover' doctrine?
What is the liability of the insurance company when a goods vehicle is used for carrying unauthorized passengers?
List the judgments specifically from the Supreme Court of India.
How is loss of dependency calculated under the multiplier method for a deceased aged 30?
